# Three-action raffle workflow contract

Base: 01d567043cbed72fb5ecef97d096fedc37da19e3. User requirement: "1 button create, 1 button approve. 1 button list. thats it". This supersedes the prior scope that retained per-operation website confirmations and normal-path Safe JSON export. Risk R3: user-intent orchestration, signatures, custody and canonical execution. Root Astra design preflight approves the bounded implementation below, subject to independent verification/review and the standing human website-release authorization.

## Integrated candidate status at source freeze

The release candidate simplifies the normal seller journey to one website activation per stage: Create, Safe Approve and List. Native wallet confirmations remain separate. Seller accounting and recovery tools are secondary disclosures. Buyer quantity, price, fees and required consents are grouped together. Refresh restores only the exact previously authorized wallet and network, without prompting or submitting. Contracts, deployed addresses and fee policy are unchanged.

Production source is frozen at `b1d2d482047d308710aca6361532a430a04e2f57`. Integration at `32c5aa669ec047f9df72b6ee270848e4a4436a09` adds only independently reviewed test changes after that source revision. The chronological builder notes below retain earlier failures and intermediate checks; they are not claims of current deployment.

## Acceptance and visible journey

The connected seller fills the existing validated NFT, title, deadline and five-tier fields and clicks Create once. Without more website prepare/review/continue clicks, the app securely saves the signed draw commitment, creates the on-chain draft, approves the exact NFT token if required, and escrows it. Each distinct wallet signature/transaction still requires the human's wallet confirmation. The visible Create consent must state the NFT will be locked and multiple wallet confirmations may follow. Never imply these are one atomic transaction. No on-chain submission happens merely by mounting or restoring a page.

The connected owner reviews the canonical NFT identity, custody, economics and draw funding facts, then clicks Approve once. Display concise adjacent language that the click confirms review of canonical collection provenance, transfer restrictions/upgradability and draw funding. The click binds all three explicit attestations to the currently displayed digest. Remove the three separate checkboxes from the normal path. Prepare and send the exact approval request through the connected Safe via the existing wallet provider. Normal approval requires no JSON export/import, copied calldata, hash paste, extra website confirmation, or unrequested SDK/account. Wallet/Safe signatures and execution remain user-controlled. Advanced recovery retains the existing manual tools.

The seller sees List after valid approval. Show the short policy/fee summary before it. Clicking List prepares and sends openWithPolicy bound to the displayed expectedPolicyHash, with no extra website confirmation. No actual opening happens without that explicit click and wallet approval.

Each successful normal path has exactly one site activation for its stage, after wallet connection/form entry. Connection and selecting an NFT are prerequisites, not additional transaction preparation screens. Exception/recovery states may require an explicit retry/resume using the same stage button. Keep old receipts/accounting/technical details disclosed secondarily; critical unresolved transactions remain prominent. Preserve artwork, brand, legal copy, buyer lifecycle, ownership policy and the current V3 deployment.

## Required invariants

1. Never bypass RaffleService's prepared-action ownership, fresh simulation, exact calldata/value/recipient, deployment attestation, connected wallet revision/account/network, journal and canonical receipt checks. Existing direct transaction path and buyer flow stay fail-closed.
2. Create orchestration is a finite explicit intent captured at the click, scoped to immutable form/draft fingerprint, seller, chain, manifest and operation generation. Session, route, unmount, changed inputs, chain/policy or invalidated draft retires stale work. No continuation may sign or submit after its scope is retired. Never recreate a failed/refreshed intent automatically.
3. Only proceed to the next create step after exact canonical success with the required two-confirmation depth and a fresh raffle/account read. Resolve created ID from the canonical manifest-address RaffleCreated log and exact create calldata. Verify seller/NFT/token/commitment and draft identity; never infer nextId or take a catalog entry by order. Replaced, reverted, unknown or inconsistent transactions stop progression. Approved token skipping requires a fresh chain read.
4. Persist signed commitment before draft transaction. Keep private commitment material out of browser persistence, URLs, logs and error reports; persist only validated public recovery identifiers and already-public draft fields needed for exact recovery. Reuse the established durable preparation recovery. A refresh cannot create a second draft or silently generate a new draw setup. An in-progress or uncertain journal blocks all new sends and uses canonical recovery first. The same Create button resumes chain-proven stages only after explicit user activation.
5. Coalesce double clicks. Storage failure before wallet invocation sends nothing. Rejection stops with no automatic retry; ambiguous post-request failures retain recovery state and prevent blind duplication. A queued async wallet request cannot outlive the user's scope. Do not clear pending data solely to enable another send.
6. Safe requests have a separate service boundary from EOA submit. Preferred API: requestOwnerExecution({prepared,wallet,beforeRequest}) constructs/validates from the service-owned PreparedAction, persists the OwnerExecutionIntent through beforeRequest before wallet dispatch, consumes the capability exactly once and requests only the exact to/data/value from the current Safe. Do not accept arbitrary reconstructed caller intents as dispatch authority. No EOA nonce or EOA transaction journal on this path.
7. Safe eth_sendTransaction returns a wallet/proposal reference, not necessarily an Ethereum transaction hash. Use a distinct typed result and never feed that result to confirmOwnerExecution/EOA receipt tracking. Start existing canonical event discovery from the persisted review block, then confirmOwnerExecution verifies the real outer transaction, exact contract/event/raffle/reviewHash/approver and generations, state, two confirmations and reorg safety. No false approval success on wallet acceptance or Safe proposal alone. Reload restores observation, never resubmission. Rejected/pre-dispatch requests can be safely retired only with proof; uncertain or accepted requests remain pending.
8. Existing Safe JSON/manual hash tools remain Advanced recovery only. Do not weaken stale-digest, wrong-owner, malformed log, rejected inner call, ownership/policy generation, revision, or canonical block checks. New one-button attestation must occur only on the explicit Approve click, never automatically when review data arrives.
9. List uses the displayed hash, then fresh preparation/submission. Any policy change rejects and requires the updated visible policy plus another explicit List click. No automatic listing after creation or owner approval.

## Design and ownership

Use the existing wallet, commitment, service, reader, outcome and disclosure modules. Add a bounded create coordinator and narrow created-ID resolver rather than duplicating low-level signing and journal logic in components. Keep new states as discriminated unions. One critical builder owns implementation and regression tests in an isolated worktree, including ports/types/service and affected UI. No dependency or schema changes expected; escalate an actual necessity to root before adding them. Existing manual V3 drafts must remain recoverable into the same Create/Approve/List sequence.

Root is the only integration/shared-release owner. Independent verification uses a separate worktree and owns only its new verification tests/evidence. Workers cannot spawn agents or agent subprocesses. Do not edit another worktree, rewrite git history, publish or submit on-chain actions. The production signature/receipt guarantees are required behavior, not optional polish.

## Required evidence

- One site click completes Create's signed durable preparation/create/approve/escrow with wallet fixtures, ordered canonical confirmations and exact token/created ID; skips only proven completed steps.
- Partial creation, reload, rejection at each stage, uncertain/hashless send, pending/replaced/reverted receipt, mismatched creation event/intent, storage failure, duplicate clicks and stale wallet/input/unmount.
- One Approve click sends exact Safe payload; returned safeTxHash is never queried as a receipt or labeled executed; proposal-only/multisig waiting, executed canonical discovery, reload, rejection, stale digest/session/owner/policy and altered target/value/data.
- One List click uses displayed policy; policy drift blocks submission and retry remains explicit.
- Existing transaction outcome/lineage/recovery, seller, buyer, owner/Safe race, admission and service-boundary regressions.
- Mobile-first browser checks at320/390/768/1440, keyboard access and no clipped primary controls. Test200% zoom and RTL mirror if tooling permits; distinguish unavailable native devices from simulated viewport evidence.
- Aggregate web tests, TypeScript, production build, contract regressions/fuzz via existing CI, fresh independent Astra final review and Claude source review. Retain failed attempts and bind final results to exact revisions.

Website main publication is already authorized after all gates pass. No contract deployment/funding/wallet signing/permission expansion is part of this implementation. Do not call live Safe prompts or the entire testnet lifecycle verified by headless fixtures alone.

## Approved wallet restoration addendum

The user reported that the seller wallet disconnects on every refresh. Root Astra approved a bounded R2 follow-up. The installed AppKit1.8.19 base client disconnects persisted WalletConnect sessions when reconnect is disabled; its Ethers adapter's syncConnection requests accounts when reconnect is enabled. Restoration therefore needs a read-only override, not a flag change alone.

Restore only a prior explicit connection matching a validated nonsecret marker scoped to origin, project, deployment and version. Require the exact SDK connector, account and Sepolia chain, plus an unexpired authorized WalletConnect namespace where applicable. Permit only account/chain reads and existing session inspection during restore. Never open a chooser or request accounts, switching, signatures or transactions. Disable fallback-first-connector restoration. Disconnect, cancellation and cross-tab marker changes retire delayed restoration. A failure leaves the app disconnected and does not destroy an unrelated wallet session. Existing users may connect once to establish the marker. Relevant acceptance checks include actual installed-SDK lifecycle behavior and callback races; root owns independent review and release.

Wallet restore implementation evidence: `restore-regressions-fourth.log` passes 61 focused tests. `restore-sdk-first.log` exercises the actual AppKit 1.8.19 constructor, initialization, controllers, existing-connection dispatcher, account synchronization and Ethers adapter; only network/DOM discovery, identity and balance lookup are fixtures. The provider traps all methods except `eth_accounts` and `eth_chainId`. Existing actual UniversalProvider cleanup/orchestration tests still pass. `restore-types-fourth.log` passes TypeScript. A prior concurrent typecheck collided with Next regenerating its type files; the failed log is retained.

Disconnect writes a per-generation sessionStorage revocation record before localStorage deletion, with local replacement as a fallback. This suppresses the old generation on same-tab reload when deletion fails. New explicit successful connection writes a new generation. If both stores refuse all mutation, the current session still disconnects and reports that the browser could not save the change; persistence is impossible under that condition. Disposal retires pending restoration and public restore becomes inert. Local fixtures now follow the same no-consent startup rule as production.

The first browser reload check exposed the old local fixture constructor attaching its injected provider before consent; that was repaired. `restore-browser-first.log` retains the failure. The second reload browser run is pending at this checkpoint. Run it with `RUN_WALLET_RESTORE_BROWSER=1 npm test -- --run test/wallet-restoration.browser.test.ts` in `web`. Independent verification, fresh review and release remain root-owned.

Wallet reload follow-up: `restore-browser-second.log` PASS, one real browser test covering two reloads with only account/network reads and no restoration after consent removal. `owner-recovery-aggregate-first.log` PASS, 46 ordinary test files and 555 tests. The prior aggregate failure was limited to the deployment-registry fake window lacking storage-event APIs; its fixture now models them. Independent verification identified missing WalletConnect namespace event validation; restore now also requires both `accountsChanged` and `chainChanged`, with a regression in the installed-SDK suite. `restore-followup-focused.log` PASS, 28 relevant tests.

Root approved two owner recovery repairs. Advanced now exposes Review and download call with the combined human attestation and current digest. It freshly prepares and exports, never sends. An unchanged exact call retains its original persisted observation block. A changed digest requires the current service-validated intent, exact original stored-value match under Web Locks, and verified public archival of the old intent before replacing it. Storage failures prevent download and leave the previous observation active. Manual canonical confirmation retires only an in-flight read-only discovery operation; late discovery cannot overwrite or release the user's new confirmation operation. Normal Approve remains one click.

`owner-recovery-types-second.log` PASS. The first targeted browser run failed because its new fixture checked Connect visibility before the page finished loading; failures are retained. The fixture now waits for the connection or approval control. The second run includes reload, changed-digest archival/storage failure, stale wallet, deferred discovery, and the existing Safe handoff suite; it is pending at this checkpoint. Root owns independent verification and final review of these repairs.

Recovery follow-up: the second browser run found that parsed owner intents and service-produced intents serialize their fields in a different order. Recovery now captures the literal stored value at click time, validates both intents through the canonical parser, and compares that exact captured value again under the lock. This retains concurrent-tab protection without rejecting a valid reloaded intent. `owner-recovery-types-third.log` PASS. The second browser run also required explicit reconnection after the fixture changed from seller to owner without changing the saved consent, plus waiting for a held test route to finish before removing it. Its failed evidence remains. The third browser run is pending at this checkpoint.

Independent review identified a delayed provider rejection after a manual recovery call had been exposed, including in another tab. Root approved a durable exact-intent manual-exposure marker under the existing owner Web Lock. Download, clipboard and raw-call display now persist and verify that marker before exposing executable fields. Definite-rejection cleanup acquires the same lock and retains observation when a matching marker exists or persistence/parse checks fail. A second tab's manual export therefore cannot be erased by the first tab's late 4001. No marker and a definite rejection still retires the record for an explicit retry. The original review block is unchanged.

Independent verification also reproduced a Create busy-state deadlock when pending NFT selection changed the scope during preparation. SellerDraftForm and CompleteCreate now retain operation ownership and prevent a new attempt until the old operation settles. At settlement, the matching operation releases its lock and changes only a still-busy stale-generation UI into a recoverable error. Existing assertIntent guards still prevent stale sends. The verifier owns the independent browser reproductions for both screens.

Observed final builder checks for this repair: `owner-exposure-browser-first.log` PASS, ten headless browser cases including cross-tab delayed rejection and ordinary rejection retry; `repair-final-types.log` PASS; `repair-final-aggregate.log` PASS, 46 ordinary files / 555 tests, 38 opt-in files / 226 tests skipped. Earlier eight-case recovery browser run also passed in `owner-recovery-browser-third.log`. These are builder results, not independent approval or deployment evidence. Root owns integration, independent gates and release.


## Claude recovery repair preflight and candidate

Root approved the bounded B1/B2/B3/B4 repair after triage against f7113fc. Submission now persists Create's checkpoint only inside the service journal lock, after the journal exists and before provider dispatch. The checkpoint includes journal id, nonce, exact transaction intent hash and start block. A proven non-dispatch callback retires the matching Create marker before the service removes its journal. If storage refuses both persistence and cleanup, recovery stays blocked with its journal retained. An exact pending-intent match can adopt a journal written before the Create callback completed. Unrelated journals cannot be adopted.

Create accepts a successful same-payload speedup only after canonical checks. A reverted transaction or different same-nonce cancellation retires only the saved pending step, preserves its public terminal receipt and stops. The next Create activation freshly prepares the stage. Advanced hash recovery observes and reconciles only; it cannot send. A legacy unknown custody send without a nonce checkpoint cannot be retired using an arbitrary hash. Exact canonical creation evidence can still recover a created draft.

Advanced Start over and edit details is restricted to a preparing record or an unsent draft with no id, creation hash or pending step. It waits for the existing operation to settle, takes the Create lock, verifies the exact saved record and absence of a global wallet journal, archives public data and restores editable fields. It never silently regenerates a preparation. A delayed server preparation response may leave an unused reserve, but no retired callback can submit it. The signed preparation deadline is checked again before POST. No server schema or authorization changes were made.

Create captures both the active stored value and a durable generation at activation. It checks both after acquiring the lock. New setup, completion and explicit retirement advance that generation, preventing a queued second tab from starting after a null-to-null completion. Storage failures stop the action. The post-journal await also rechecks the captured form scope.

Proven Safe non-dispatch/rejection cleanup now compares the exact intent and manual-exposure marker under the owner lock even after unmount or wallet revision change. Only UI updates remain tied to the component scope. File export and wallet-request handoffs have different states and public channel metadata; unknown legacy handoffs receive import instructions. Revocation explicitly instructs the owner to import, sign and execute the file. A download alone is never described as a pending Safe request.

Evidence-only review findings: production LiveSeller, LiveSellerRaffle and LiveRaffle already forwarded both SaveCommitment arguments at the reviewed candidate. Automatic private preparation uses 32 bytes from crypto.getRandomValues and fails closed if unavailable. Native Enter form submission remains an explicit user action. Lagging post-step reads still fail safely rather than granting success, so no reader refactor was added. Edit-form copy now describes updating rather than locking the NFT.

Initial repair checks: `claude-repair-chain-second.log` PASS, nine real local-chain cases including cancellation and explicit retry at each Create stage and checkpoint callback failure. The first run retained a memory journal between tests after deliberately refusing every recovery write; each case now has an isolated service journal. `claude-repair-types-fourth.log` PASS. Earlier compile failures and the first chain failure remain in the artifact directory. Browser, additional recovery cases and aggregate checks remain pending for this initial candidate. Root owns independent verification and fresh review; this record is not an approval.

Follow-up to 39ca1ea: independent verification reproduced a property-order comparison that made immediate unsent-draft reset depend on reload. Create records now use one canonical serializer for writes and semantic identity comparisons. Review also found that a failed primary Safe storage write could leave the UI preparing after a proven non-dispatch. Cleanup now recognizes an absent active record as retired, preserves exact-record/exposure checks for existing records, and always settles the visible attempt without replacing an already-confirmed execution. Automatic canonical owner success clears discovery-operation ownership; CompleteCreate leaves busy state after successful completion even if its parent does not remount.

Additional observed checks: `claude-repair-chain-third.log` PASS, 12 local-chain tests including a real exact reverted approval, exact crash-gap journal adoption, Advanced hash recovery without another send, and rejection of unrelated journals. `claude-repair-recovery-unit-second.log` PASS, 15 unit checks including public-only reset archival, pending/known-chain guards, stale scope, archive failure, completed null-to-null generations and expired signatures before POST. `claude-repair-types-fifth.log` PASS. `claude-repair-aggregate-first.log` PASS, 46 files and 555 tests, before the additional tests. The first browser batch launched three Next fixtures concurrently in this worktree and failed 17 cases; its log is retained and is not acceptance evidence. A serialized rerun with `--maxWorkers=1` is in progress. No wallet files or tests were changed in this batch; root assigned that review to a separate owner.

The new Advanced reset handler also follows the existing operation-owned busy-release rule: a wallet/input generation change cannot leave its settled operation visibly busy or permit an overlapping retry. `claude-repair-focused-final.log` PASS, 27 combined coordinator/service/reset/API checks; `claude-repair-types-sixth.log` PASS. The serialized browser run remains in progress at this source freeze.

Serialized browser result for the recovery candidate: `claude-repair-browser-second.log` completed with exit 1. All seven owner-recovery tests and all four Safe handoff tests passed, including file revocation instructions after reload/re-download, manual exposure across tabs, delayed rejection, stale wallet, archival failure and canonical confirmation priority. The legacy seller-portal suite passed one case and failed nine. Its first failure waits for `26 total` after a helper conditionally clicks Connect using an immediate visibility check; later failures wait for seller-only forms and headings. This supports a fixture hydration/connection diagnosis, but no DOM-state proof is claimed. Root owns that legacy suite on the integrated UI candidate and requested no further broad reruns here. All fixtures exited. Required independent verification, final integrated checks, review and release remain root-owned.
